security.note: digest defines NO own res.groups; 4 access rules gate digest.digest + digest.tip on base.group_erp_manager (full CRUD) vs base.group_user (read-only). Unsubscribe is authorized out-of-band by an hmac token (_get_unsubscribe_token), not by ACL.

behavioral_notes.observation: Daily cron 'Digest Emails' (ir_cron_digest_scheduler_action) runs model._cron_send_digest_email(), which searches digests with next_run_date <= today and state='activated', then per digest iterates digest.user_ids and calls _action_send_to_user(user) for EACH subscriber individually (one mail.mail per recipient, rendered in the user's lang/company). After sending it advances next_run_date by the periodicity delta (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly via _get_next_run_date). _check_daily_logs inspects res.users.log: if no recipient logged in within the window, the digest is added to to_slowdown and its periodicity is bumped down one step (_get_next_periodicity: daily->weekly->monthly->quarterly) to avoid spamming inactive users. MailDeliveryException is caught and the digest retried next cron run.

behavioral_notes.element: digest.digest._compute_kpis / _calculate_company_based_kpi (kpi_* fields over a date window)
behavioral_notes.observation: KPIs are opt-in Boolean toggle fields named kpi_*/x_kpi_*/x_studio_kpi_* (base ships kpi_res_users_connected, kpi_mail_message_total); each has a paired <field>_value computed field. _compute_kpis renders 3 columns by re-running the value compute under 3 context timeframes (Last 24h / Last 7 Days / Last 30 Days from _compute_timeframes) plus their prior periods, invalidating the cache between each to force recomputation, and derives a percentage margin vs the previous period. _calculate_company_based_kpi is the generic engine: it _read_group()s the target model (company_id/company_ids field) filtered on (date_field >= start, < end) scoped to the digest's company. kpi_mail_message_total_value directly search_count()s mail.message with subtype mail.mt_comment over the window. AccessError on any KPI silently drops that row from that user's email (per-user data security).

_action_send_to_user mints a per-(digest,user) hmac token via _get_unsubscribe_token and embeds both a body 'Unsubscribe' link (/digest/<id>/unsubscribe?token=..&user_id=..) and RFC-8058 List-Unsubscribe / List-Unsubscribe-Post=One-Click email headers pointing at /digest/<id>/unsubscribe_oneclik. The public controller validates the token with consteq (constant-time) before calling _action_unsubscribe_users (sudo removes the user from user_ids). The one-click route is POST-only + csrf=False so an MUA can unsubscribe without a session while anti-spam GET prefetch cannot. /digest/<id>/set_periodicity (auth=user) is gated to base.group_erp_manager and lets a manager switch periodicity from the email.

Each email includes tips_count tips drawn by _compute_tips: it searches digest.tip for tips NOT yet sent to this user (user_ids != user.id) whose group_id is in the user's groups or is empty, limit=tips_count. The tip_description Html is rendered with the qweb engine (mail.render.mixin) and html-sanitized. When consumed=True the user is appended to tip.user_ids, so each tip is shown at most once per recipient and tips rotate over successive digests until exhausted.

digest extends res.users.create: when ir.config_parameter digest.default_digest_emails and digest.default_digest_id are set, every newly created non-share (internal) user is automatically added to the default digest's user_ids (sudo). This is how new employees start receiving the company digest without manual subscription.

0 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, 0 asset bundles. The entire user-facing surface is server-rendered QWeb email: digest.digest_mail_layout (encapsulating HTML/CSS shell) + digest.digest_mail_main (3-column KPI grid digest.digest_tool_kpi with up/down margin badges, tips loop, manager 'customize/switch periodicity' preferences, mobile-app banner, unsubscribe footer) + the portal_digest_unsubscribed confirmation page. Backend config UI is plain form/list/search (2 form, 3 list, 2 search) on digest.digest/digest.tip.

it_architecture.application: digest (KPI Digests application component - periodic performance-reporting / summary-email engine; thin host that other apps extend with their own kpi_* fields)
logical_data_erm: digest.digest kpi_*_value -> (any model)._read_group over a date window (computed, not stored FK)
information_flows: side-effect: _cron_send_digest_email -> per subscriber _action_send_to_user -> mail.mail (one outgoing email per recipient) via mail.render.mixin

side-effect: KPI compute -> reads mail.message, res.users.log and every consumer module's models (account/crm/project/pos/sale/website_sale/im_livechat/hr_recruitment) via _read_group over Last 24h/7d/30d windows
side-effect: inactive recipient (no res.users.log in window) -> periodicity slowed one step to throttle email volume
side-effect: new internal res.users -> auto-added to default digest user_ids

inverse-dependency: 9 modules inject kpi_* Boolean toggles + paired *_value computes (crm, account, project, point_of_sale, website_sale, sale_management, im_livechat, hr_recruitment) so a single digest email aggregates cross-app KPIs

capabilities: Periodic KPI Digest Email (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly company summary)
Company Performance Metric Computation (period-over-period with % margin)
Extensible KPI Catalog (opt-in kpi_* toggles, host for other apps' metrics)
Subscriber Management & Auto-Subscription (default digest for new internal users)
Engagement-Based Send Throttling (slow down digests for inactive recipients)
Per-Recipient Unsubscribe & Preference Self-Service (hmac token, RFC-8058 one-click)
Contextual Tip / Onboarding Rotation (consume-once tips by group)
value_streams: Compute-and-Broadcast-KPIs: cron due -> compute per-company KPIs over time windows -> render per-subscriber email -> queue mail.mail -> advance next_run_date
Throttle-Inactive-Recipients: check res.users.log -> no activity -> downgrade periodicity + notify preference change
Unsubscribe-and-Tune: recipient clicks token link -> validate hmac -> remove from user_ids / manager switches periodicity
organization: (digest defines no own groups - reuses base groups via 4 access rules; recipients restricted to share=False internal users)
policies: Recipients limited to internal users (domain share=False on user_ids); share/portal users excluded
Engagement throttle: if no res.users.log for recipients in the period window, periodicity is automatically slowed one step (_check_daily_logs / _get_next_periodicity) to curb unwanted email
Unsubscribe gated by constant-time hmac token (not ACL); one-click route POST-only + csrf-exempt per RFC 8058
set_periodicity restricted to base.group_erp_manager; KPI rows the user cannot read (AccessError) are silently dropped from that user's email
Default-digest auto-subscription controlled by ir.config_parameter digest.default_digest_emails / digest.default_digest_id
stakeholders: Business manager / executive (digest recipient consuming KPIs)
ERP manager / administrator (configures digest, selects KPIs, periodicity)
Consumer modules (account/crm/project/sale/pos... extending the KPI set)
metrics: period-over-period margin % per KPI (Last 24h / 7 Days / 30 Days vs prior period)
downstream KPIs: revenue, new leads/opportunities, invoiced, POS sales, website sales, project hours, livechat/recruitment counts (injected by consumer modules)

classification.apqc_category: 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities (manage business performance / KPI reporting); secondary touch on 9.4 Manage internal controls and an information/knowledge-distribution aspect
classification.rationale: digest is a cross-cutting SUPPORT subsystem (Stabell & Fjeldstad): it has no value stream of its own, produces no product, order, or document, and converts no demand into delivered output. It is internal performance-reporting/communication infrastructure - it READS the metrics produced by primary activities (sales, invoicing, projects, POS, leads) and BROADCASTS them as a periodic summary email. Hence value_model=support / activity_class=support. APQC best fit is 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' because the dominant capability is managing/monitoring business performance via KPI reporting and dashboards - the digest is a management-information instrument that lets leadership track company health over time (period-over-period KPI margins). This is preferred over 9.4 (internal controls/governance) because digest is forward-looking performance monitoring rather than compliance/control enforcement, and it is preferred over a pure internal-communications classification (which would lean on the mail subsystem at ~13.x Information & Knowledge Management): although digest sends email, the email is merely the delivery channel - the substance and reason-for-being is the KPI/business-performance content and its extensible metric catalog, which 9.4-style internal comms does not capture. The concrete delivery mechanics (per-recipient mail.mail, unsubscribe, templates) are inherited from mail (itself support/13.x); digest adds the business-performance-management layer on top, anchoring it at 13.0. No 13.0 row exists yet in apqc_odoo_map.tsv; this is the architect classification.

standard_capabilities: Out-of-box daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly KPI digest email per company
Two base KPIs (connected users, messages sent) with period-over-period margins across 3 timeframes
Opt-in KPI selection per digest via kpi_* Boolean toggles (no code to enable/disable a metric)
Per-recipient send in recipient language/company; one-click + token unsubscribe (RFC 8058)
Automatic periodicity slow-down for inactive recipients (anti-spam)
Auto-subscription of new internal users to a default digest
Rotating, group-scoped onboarding tips consumed once per user
Extension point used by account/crm/project/sale/pos/website_sale/im_livechat/hr_recruitment to add their own KPIs
typical_fits: Enable the default 'Your Odoo Periodic Digest' and let new employees auto-subscribe
Toggle which KPIs appear and set company-wide periodicity from Settings
Add a custom KPI by declaring a kpi_<x> Boolean + kpi_<x>_value compute that calls _calculate_company_based_kpi
Switch a manager from daily to weekly straight from the email footer
common_gaps: KPIs are integer/monetary counts over a fixed company date-window - no charts/trends, grouping, or drill-down beyond the optional 'Open Report' action link
Custom KPIs require Python (compute method) or Studio x_kpi_* fields; non-trivial metrics not configurable by end users
Audience is per-digest user list (internal only) - no role/segment targeting, A/B content, or external/portal recipients without dev
Single delivery channel (email via mail.mail/ir.mail_server); no in-app dashboard, Slack/Teams push, or scheduled PDF
Engagement throttle is coarse (presence in res.users.log), not open/click tracking
